key_insight: A vorticity-augmented supervised model best reconstructs turbulent flows at lower sparsity, while a physics-informed PINN is more stable when labels are scarce and extrapolation is harder.
engineering_relevance: The work points to practical routes for compressing large Navier--Stokes simulation datasets and recovering useful flow fields from sparse measurements in turbulence applications.
method: Supervised reconstruction with vorticity augmentation to recover velocity fields from sparse inputs.
Partially assisted compressible PINN based on the 3D unsteady compressible Navier--Stokes equations.
Compare both methods across sparsity levels using spectral, statistical, and coherent-structure metrics.
evidence_signal: Performance was assessed with instantaneous velocity fields, mean-squared error, energy spectra, Reynolds stresses, turbulent kinetic energy, and Q-criterion isosurfaces across multiple sparsity levels.
watch_item: The approaches are regime-dependent, so neither method is universally superior and the PINN may require careful training to maintain accuracy on highly turbulent, sparse data.
paper_title: SCoReT: Super-Resolution Compression and Reconstruction of Turbulent Flows
